commands.version: Print the installed software and contract version.
commands.doctor: Inspect local runtime, catalog, storage and graph prerequisites.
commands.search: Search indexed recording text and relationships using a normalized query.
commands.workspace init: Create a fresh library using local filesystem, SQLite and LadybugDB defaults.
commands.workspace plan: Normalize explicit nonsecret backend selections without creating a library.
commands.workspace preflight: Probe an elected backend plan without provisioning its target directory.
commands.workspace provision: Create a fresh library from a backend plan and reconcile an immutable retry.
commands.workspace show: Read the selected library configuration and current runtime identity.
commands.runtime serve: Host the shared noninteractive runtime for local clients.
commands.credentials select: Select the native, encrypted vault or runtime-session credential backend.
commands.credentials add: Store a new credential without replacing an existing identity.
commands.credentials replace: Replace the value of an existing credential.
commands.credentials delete: Delete an existing credential from the selected backend.
commands.credentials status: Inspect stored and unlocked state without revealing a credential value.
commands.credentials unlock: Unlock an encrypted vault for the current runtime owner.
commands.credentials load: Load protected vault or session credentials for the current runtime owner.
commands.catalog show: Read the catalog identity, schema and revision state.
commands.catalog migrate: Migrate an existing catalog under exclusive library ownership.
commands.catalog export: Write a portable catalog snapshot to a new file.
commands.catalog restore: Restore a portable catalog snapshot under exclusive ownership.
commands.jobs start: Start a cancellable synthetic job for a duration in milliseconds.
commands.jobs show: Read a durable job and its current attempt.
commands.jobs history: Read job attempt generations after an optional generation number.
commands.jobs cancel: Request cancellation of a durable job.
commands.jobs retry: Retry an eligible failed or cancelled job.
commands.artifacts publish: Publish immutable file bytes through the selected artifact store.
commands.artifacts show: Read an artifact publication receipt and lifecycle state.
commands.artifacts verify: Verify the stored bytes against the immutable publication receipt.
commands.artifacts materialize: Acquire a local materialization and its returned lease identity.
commands.artifacts reconcile: Resume or reconcile an interrupted publication.
commands.artifacts retire: Retire a publication after its references and leases allow it.
commands.artifacts cache-prune: Prune an eligible local cached materialization.
commands.artifacts retain: Add an explicit caller-owned publication reference.
commands.artifacts release-reference: Remove an explicit caller-owned publication reference.
commands.backup create: Create a portable backup and retain its referenced publications.
commands.backup show: Inspect a backup directory without opening its catalog.
commands.backup verify: Verify a backup directory and its referenced bytes.
commands.backup restore: Restore a backup directory into the selected compatible library.
commands.backup release: Release a backup retention reference using its directory or backup identity.
commands.pipelines show: Read one processing pipeline and its revision.
commands.pipelines set: Create or update a revision-checked processing pipeline.
commands.pipelines inspect: Inspect a pipeline against current recording and processing prerequisites.
commands.speakers show: Read a speaker identity and revision.
commands.speakers set: Create or update a revision-checked speaker identity.
commands.speakers aliases: Read the aliases belonging to one speaker.
commands.speakers select: Select timed speaker audio evidence from across the library.
commands.speakers diagnostics: Inspect available speaker evidence and matching diagnostics.
commands.terms show: Read a controlled vocabulary term and revision.
commands.terms set: Create or update a revision-checked controlled vocabulary term.
commands.terms compile: Compile the selected vocabulary into its runtime representation.
commands.import-presets create: Create a reusable import policy with a unique identity and name.
commands.import-presets show: Read a preset by UUID or exact saved name.
commands.import-presets update: Update a preset using its current revision.
commands.import-presets delete: Delete a preset using its current revision.
commands.setup location: Preview an absolute library directory without creating it.
commands.setup provision: Provision the saved pre-library draft and its selected credential backend.
commands.setup show: Read the optional setup journey and command-line next actions.
commands.setup save: Save optional setup progress with the current revision and observation proofs.
commands.setup readiness: Probe current task prerequisites independently of saved setup progress.
commands.setup draft show: Read the private pre-library setup draft.
commands.setup draft save: Save an absolute target and backend plan before library creation.
commands.settings setup: Reopen the optional setup journey for the selected library.
commands.settings show: Read settings sections, values and revision tokens.
commands.settings set: Save a settings section using its exact current revision token.
commands.media tools: Import a pinned media-tools JSON configuration effective on the next operation.
commands.media import: Admit source media or a manifest and enqueue the elected processing.
commands.media list: List accepted media entries using recording identities.
commands.media show: Read the current media authority and revision.
commands.media metadata: Read the captured source metadata summary.
commands.media refresh: Refresh captured observations and elected processing for accepted media.
commands.media set-origin: Correct recording date provenance with an explicit current revision.
commands.media relocate: Change a legacy referenced source location with its current revision.
commands.media capture: Read a bounded metadata, facts or dates byte page.
commands.media playback: Acquire a bounded playback descriptor and lease.
commands.media playback-check: Check whether a playback descriptor still names current bytes.
commands.media playback-close: Release an acquired playback descriptor and lease.
commands.processing tools: Import a pinned processing-tools JSON configuration effective on the next operation.
commands.processing readiness: Probe elected processing prerequisites without starting inference.
commands.workers catalog: List the bundled worker environment recipes.
commands.workers inspect: Inspect a worker environment against its exact recipe.
commands.workers plan: Plan an elected worker environment without creating it.
commands.workers setup: Create an explicitly elected pinned worker environment as durable work.
commands.transcript import: Attach one transcript or a per-item transcript manifest to existing recordings.
commands.recordings show: Read recording authority, transcript identity and attribution state.
commands.recordings document: Read a bounded page of the current transcript document.
commands.recordings mappings: List speaker-mapping rows using their returned row UUID cursor.
commands.recordings process: Enqueue elected recording processing through its selected pipeline.
commands.recordings assemble: Assemble the current recording transcript and speaker attribution.
commands.recordings map-speaker: Correct one native/local speaker mapping using current authority.
commands.recordings match: Elect voice matching against configured speaker profiles.
commands.recordings export: Export the selected recording transcript to a new destination.
commands.recordings resolve-segment: Resolve a current cue or speaker segment into timed media.
commands.recordings cues: Read current transcript cues after a returned cue identity.
commands.recordings roster show: Read the recording known-speaker roster and revision.
commands.recordings roster add: Add repeatable known speakers to a revision-checked roster.
commands.recordings roster remove: Remove repeatable known speakers from a revision-checked roster.
commands.recordings roster replace: Replace the known-speaker roster with the elected speaker list.
commands.recordings roster clear: Clear the known-speaker roster using its current revision.
commands.work list: List durable work acceptance and completion states.
commands.work show: Read one durable work item and its current state.
commands.work results: Read durable work results after a returned numeric ordinal.
commands.work wait: Wait for durable work completion for a bounded interval.
commands.work retry: Retry eligible failed or cancelled durable work.
commands.models register: Register immutable base-model identity and manifest as durable work.
commands.models acquire: Acquire and verify an immutable model manifest as durable work.
commands.models download: Acquire and verify an immutable model manifest (alias of acquire).
commands.models list: List registered base-model identities and readiness.
commands.models show: Read a registered model and immutable manifest.
commands.models verify: Verify acquired model files and current readiness.
commands.models materialize: Materialize acquired model files and return explicit leases.
commands.models base register: Register immutable base-model identity and manifest as durable work.
commands.models base acquire: Acquire and verify an immutable model manifest as durable work.
commands.models base download: Acquire and verify an immutable model manifest (alias of acquire).
commands.models base list: List registered base-model identities and readiness.
commands.models base show: Read a registered model and immutable manifest.
commands.models base verify: Verify acquired model files and current readiness.
commands.models base materialize: Materialize acquired model files and return explicit leases.
commands.models defaults: Read default model selections without starting acquisition.
commands.models prepare: Enqueue an elected model preparation plan.
commands.models resolve: Resolve a model UUID, immutable name/version or alias for an operation.
commands.models discover: Read a configured model source catalog without adopting a new route.
commands.models train: Enqueue optional speaker-associated model training against an immutable dataset.
commands.models alias list: List configured model alias records and revisions.
commands.models alias show: Read one configured model alias record.
commands.models alias set: Create or update a model alias with an explicit expected revision.
commands.models alias remove: Remove an existing model alias using its positive current revision.
commands.models source list: List configured model source records and revisions.
commands.models source show: Read one configured model source record.
commands.models source set: Create or update a model source with an explicit expected revision.
commands.models source remove: Remove an existing model source using its positive current revision.
commands.models dataset list: List immutable training datasets with an optional JSON cursor.
commands.models speaker list: List speaker-associated model versions with an optional JSON cursor.
commands.models dataset create: Capture a new immutable speaker training dataset from elected evidence.
commands.models speaker fetch: Fetch verified speaker-model bytes to a new elected directory.
commands.models profile set: Select a compatible speaker-model version using the current profile revision.
commands.graph capabilities: Read the selected graph backend query capabilities.
commands.graph status: Read graph publication revisions and pending state.
commands.graph publish: Publish current catalog evidence to the selected graph backend.
commands.graph rebuild: Rebuild derived graph evidence from retained catalog authority.
commands.evidence extract: Extract retained evidence for one recording using elected limits.
commands.evidence show: Read retained evidence for one recording.
commands.query services: Inspect candidate query-assistance services without adopting routes or loading models.
commands.query assistance-test: Run an elected synthetic query-assistance task for exact saved settings.
commands.query assist: Request a normalized query suggestion using the selected assistance route.
commands.query assistance-show: Read selected query-assistance settings and revision.
commands.query assistance-set: Save query-assistance settings with their current revision.
commands.query run: Execute an explicit normalized/native definition or saved query.
commands.query explain: Explain an explicit definition or saved query without mutation.
commands.query show: Read one saved query and revision.
commands.query save: Create or update a saved query with its current revision.
commands.query validate: Validate a query definition without executing it.
commands.query native: Execute a read-only native query file in the selected backend dialect.
commands.timeline calendar: Read recording dates grouped by an elected timezone and filter.
commands.timeline recording: Read the evidence timeline of one recording.
commands.views show: Read one saved view and revision.
commands.views save: Create or update a revision-checked saved view.

--workspace.meaning: Select the library directory; relative paths resolve from the process working directory.
--workspace.default: discover from the working directory unless supplied
--workspace.conditions: global; not required by pre-library operations

--request-id.meaning: Correlation UUID; preserve it with immutable input to reconcile an unknown mutation outcome.

--json.meaning: Emit the complete versioned response envelope.

--verbose.meaning: Add request and library identifiers to human output.

--quiet.meaning: Suppress informational human output and progress; preserve warnings and errors.

--log-file.meaning: Elect private rotating JSONL diagnostics, at most 1 MiB and two predecessors.
--log-file.conditions: parent directory must exist; excludes private input values

--help.meaning: Describe this command without reading input, discovering a library or starting work.

-h.meaning: Describe this command before performing work.

--version.meaning: Print the software and contract version.

--input.meaning: Read a complete JSON document from a file, without a runtime-request envelope.
--input.conditions: never inline JSON; see the template and complete input contract

--manifest.meaning: Read per-item media/transcript selections from a JSON or CSV manifest.
--manifest.conditions: transcript batch excludes a positional transcript, --record and --legacy-sidecar

--title.meaning: Set the admitted recording display title.
--title.conditions: one title per invocation; per-item manifest titles can differ

--record.meaning: Select an existing recording by UUID or exact title for transcript attachment.
--record.default: new media admission for media import
--record.conditions: required for single transcript import; excludes transcript --manifest

--transcript.meaning: Attach the elected transcript source path or URL.

--subtitle.meaning: Attach the elected transcript source path or URL.

--credential-id.meaning: Use the selected source-acquisition credential UUID without placing its value in arguments.
--credential-id.conditions: must exist in the selected credential backend

--acquisition-adapter.meaning: Choose the configured acquisition adapter identity.
--acquisition-adapter.default: direct HTTP acquisition for a URL

--acquisition-max-bytes.meaning: Bound remote source acquisition in bytes.
--acquisition-max-bytes.default: 68719476736 bytes (64 GiB), unless overridden by the elected policy
--acquisition-max-bytes.conditions: positive byte count; applies to remote media

--acquisition-timeout-ms.default: 600000 milliseconds (10 minutes), unless overridden by the elected policy
--acquisition-timeout-ms.conditions: positive duration; applies to remote media

--originated-at.meaning: Record an owner-provided RFC3339 instant, preserving explicit provenance.

--originated-on.meaning: Record an owner-provided YYYY-MM-DD calendar date without inventing a time.

--originated-earliest.meaning: Set the earliest RFC3339 instant of an uncertain date range.
--originated-earliest.conditions: excludes exact/date-only forms; must not follow latest bound

--originated-latest.meaning: Set the latest RFC3339 instant of an uncertain date range.
--originated-latest.conditions: excludes exact/date-only forms; must not precede earliest bound

--timezone.meaning: Interpret local recording dates in an IANA zone, local zone or explicit offset.
--timezone.conditions: use local, UTC, America/New_York or +02:00; ambiguity needs an explicit fold/gap policy

--dst-fold.meaning: Select the earlier or later instant in a repeated local clock interval.
--dst-fold.conditions: applies only to an ambiguous local timestamp

--dst-gap.meaning: Shift a nonexistent local clock time forward by the gap.
--dst-gap.conditions: applies only to a nonexistent local timestamp

--date-precedence.meaning: Choose which retained date observations establish recording authority.
--date-precedence.conditions: owner, embedded and filesystem observations retain their provenance

--preset.meaning: Apply an import preset by UUID or exact saved name.
--preset.default: configured default preset, otherwise explicit options
--preset.conditions: CLI values override per-item values, which override manifest defaults and preset choices

--pipeline-id.meaning: Elect a saved processing pipeline UUID after admission.

--no-pipeline.meaning: Admit media without enqueuing a processing pipeline.

--destination-profile.meaning: Elect a configured canonical-storage destination profile UUID.
--destination-profile.conditions: the configured route is reused without repeated review

--attribution.meaning: Choose native attribution, diarization, automatic selection or off.
--attribution.conditions: diarize requires an elected diarization route/model

--transcript-format.meaning: Declare the external transcript format when it cannot be inferred.

--transcript-credential-id.meaning: Use a selected credential UUID for transcript acquisition.
--transcript-credential-id.conditions: credential values remain in the credential backend

--transcript-adapter.meaning: Choose the configured transcript acquisition adapter.

--transcript-max-bytes.conditions: positive byte count, at most 16 MiB

--transcript-timeout-ms.default: 120000 milliseconds (2 minutes), unless overridden by the elected policy

--subtitle-stream-index.meaning: Select an embedded subtitle stream by zero-based index.
--subtitle-stream-index.conditions: 0 is an explicit selection; applies to embedded subtitles

--subtitle-language.meaning: Select an embedded subtitle language tag.
--subtitle-language.conditions: use the source stream language; explicit stream index takes the exact stream

--diarization-model-id.conditions: required when no compatible diarization default is configured

--known-speaker.meaning: Add a known-speaker UUID to the elected recording roster.
--known-speaker.conditions: repeatable; each value is a library speaker identity

--existing-transcript.meaning: Retain, clear or replace the current transcript during audio replacement.
--existing-transcript.conditions: replacement requires the elected transcript and applicability decision

--existing-roster.meaning: Retain or clear the current known-speaker roster during audio replacement.

--revision.meaning: Select the exact current revision or saved-query revision.
--revision.conditions: required by revision-checked media changes; positive integer

--after.meaning: Continue after the preceding page cursor.
--after.conditions: reuse unchanged filters; UUID for media/work/base-model lists, opaque cursor for search

--after-ordinal.meaning: Continue work results after the returned numeric result ordinal.
--after-ordinal.conditions: nonnegative integer; use this option rather than --after

--limit.meaning: Bound the number of returned page items.

--speaker.meaning: Filter by a library speaker UUID, or elect roster members.
--speaker.conditions: repeatable only for recording roster mutations

--media.meaning: Filter results by a recording/media UUID.
--media.conditions: library recording identity, not a source file path

--dialect.meaning: Select the exact backend-native read-only query dialect.

--file.meaning: Read the native query statement from a UTF-8 file.
--file.conditions: one supported read statement; relative path resolves from the working directory

--parameters.meaning: Read typed native query parameters from a JSON file.
--parameters.conditions: unique object members; exact integers are preserved

--saved.conditions: excludes --input; optional --revision selects the saved revision

--operation.meaning: Resolve a model for the elected operation.

--expected-revision.meaning: Apply a change against the observed current revision.
--expected-revision.conditions: 0 creates an absent record only where supported; deletion requires a positive current revision

--destination.meaning: Write fetched speaker-model bytes to a new elected directory.
--destination.conditions: destination must not overwrite existing bytes

--mode.meaning: Choose a self-contained or reference-only backup.

--credential-backend.meaning: Select the credential provider for new provisioning.
--credential-backend.default: saved setup draft choice, otherwise native
--credential-backend.conditions: native|vault|session; immutable retries reuse the same selection

--timeout-ms.meaning: Wait for completion for this many milliseconds.
--timeout-ms.conditions: timeout leaves work running; inspect, wait again or cancel

--copy.meaning: Admit canonical bytes using managed storage.

--reference.conditions: excludes --copy; new admission requires managed canonical audio and does not retain original paths as authority

--local-http.meaning: Explicitly allow the elected loopback HTTP fixture/service source.
--local-http.conditions: does not elect an unconfigured external route

--new-entry.meaning: Create a distinct recording even when source identity matches an existing entry.

--replace-audio.meaning: Replace accepted audio after verifying the new canonical authority.
--replace-audio.conditions: requires an existing recording target and preserves accepted authority until commit

--transcript-applies.meaning: Confirm that the retained/elected transcript applies to replacement audio.
--transcript-applies.conditions: used with audio replacement and transcript-retention policy

--replace-transcript.meaning: Replace the existing accepted transcript with the elected input.
--replace-transcript.conditions: requires an existing recording and new transcript input

--legacy-sidecar.meaning: Read a supported historical sidecar for an existing recording.
--legacy-sidecar.conditions: requires --record; excludes a positional transcript and --manifest

--secret-input.meaning: Read a bounded protected credential object from stdin.
--secret-input.conditions: required when the elected backend plan needs secrets; never put secret values in arguments

--diarization-device.meaning: Select auto, cpu or cuda for local transcript attribution; auto/cuda permit one observable CPU fallback.
--diarization-device.default: auto for new local diarization work
--diarization-device.conditions: used with diarized attribution; explicit cpu stays CPU
